name: Depth 2.5D
summary: A top-down world with a near side and a far side: one depth rule, and walls whose picture has height while their collider does not.
description: A flat top-down game gives each kind of thing a fixed depth, so a wall is always behind the player or always in front, and it reads as a diagram. This replaces that with one rule -- flat things keep a band, standing things sort by where their feet are -- and the extrusion that goes with it. Height is a pivot trick: one sprite sized [w, h + height] and hung upward from the footprint, so the picture rises and the collider never moves. Comes with the flat bands, cap tracking so a demolished wall takes its roof with it, and the four failures that are invisible to every gate: orphaned top faces, overlays parked inside the standing band, footprints read off the extruded sprite, and extruded things that rotate.
nextSteps: Put Depth25D.js on a manager actor and tag it Depth.
Set worldSize to your map's tallest coordinate -- everything else is a ratio of it.
Build scenery through standing() and floors through flat(), instead of creating sprites directly.
Put StandUpright.js on anything that moves; static things are depthed once when built.
Move any full-screen overlay to overlayBand() -- 0.8 is now the middle of the world.
Destroy standing actors with demolish(), or their top faces stay in the air.
